ex-E301-1.title: End-use energy efficiency of a kettle
ex-E301-1.question:
A 2200-W electric kettle heats 1.5 kg of water with an initial temperature of 25 °C. The water starts to boil in 4 minutes.

(a) Find the energy input into the electric kettle.

(b) Find the useful energy output of the electric kettle.

(c) Find the end-use energy efficiency of the electric kettle.

Given: specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J kg−1 °C−1
ex-E301-1.answer:
(a) Energy input Ein = Pt

= 2200 × (4 × 60)

= 528 000 J

(b) Useful energy output Eout = mcΔT

= 1.5 × 4200 × (100 − 25)

= 472 500 J

(c) End-use energy efficiency = EoutEin × 100%

= 472 500528 000 × 100%

= 89.5%
ex-E301-1.tips:
Tip

The useful energy for an electric kettle is the energy absorbed by the water.
ex-E301-1.location: Book E3  |  Chapter E301  |  Source PDF p. 4

ex-E301-2.question:

(a) Estimate the cost of electricity in operating the television for 1460 hours. The cost of electricity is $1.1 per kW h.

(b) Estimate the input power of the television.
ex-E301-2.answer:

ex-E301-3.title: Energy output of a microwave oven
ex-E301-3.question:
(a) A 800-W microwave oven takes time t to heat 0.3 kg of potato from

4 °C to 50 °C. The end-use energy efficiency of the oven is 55% in this process. Find t. The specific heat capacity of the potato is 3400 J kg−1 °C−1.

(b) Paul suggests using an induction cooker since it has a high end-use energy efficiency. He immerses the potato in a pot of water and puts the pot on the induction cooker operating at 800 W. However, he finds that the actual time taken to heat the potato is much longer. Why?
ex-E301-3.answer:
(a) Energy needed E = mcΔT = 0.3 × 3400 × (50 − 4) = 46 920 J

Useful power output Pout = Pin × ηend = 800 × 55% = 440 W

t=EPout=46 920440=107 s

(b) Extra energy is required to heat the pot and the water. The amount of extra energy is large because water has a high specific heat capacity.
ex-E301-3.tips:
Tip

By E = Pt , t = EP

P here is the rate of energy transferred to the potato and is the useful power output.
ex-E301-3.location: Book E3  |  Chapter E301  |  Source PDF p. 17

ex-E301-4.title: Running cost
ex-E301-4.question: Daisy finds that the end-use energy efficiency of an electric hotplate is 72%. On average, 5.4 MJ of energy is needed for cooking each day. Calculate the cost of electricity per day for using the electric hotplate. The cost of electricity is $1.1 per kW h.
ex-E301-4.tips:
Tip

Remember to convert J to kW h.

1 kW h = 1000 W × 3600 s

= (1000 × 3600) J

ex-E301-5.title: Cooling capacity
ex-E301-5.question:
An air conditioner of cooling capacity 1.2 kW is installed in an empty room of dimensions 3 m × 3 m × 2.5 m. It is turned on for 3 minutes. The specific heat capacity of air is 1000 J kg−1 °C−1 and the density of air is 1.2 kg m−3.

(a) Find the amount of heat that the air conditioner removes from the room.

(b) Estimate the temperature drop of the air in the room.

(c) The actual temperature drop of the air in the room is smaller than that estimated in (b). Give one reason.
ex-E301-5.answer:
(a) Amount of heat removed

= cooling capacity × time = 1200 × (3 × 60) = 2.16 × 105 J

(b) Mass of air in the room

= 1.2 × (3 × 3 × 2.5) = 27 kg

By Q = mcΔT,

ΔT = Qmc = 2.16 × 10527 × 1000 = 8 °C

The temperature drop is 8 °C.

(c) Heat may be transferred from the outside to the room through walls. / Heat has to be removed from walls.
ex-E301-5.location: Book E3  |  Chapter E301  |  Source PDF p. 27

ex-E301-6.title: COP
ex-E301-6.question:
The COP of a 1500-W air conditioner is 2.3.

(a) Find the amount of heat that it can remove from a room in 1 minute.

(b) Find the rate at which heat is being released to the outside.
ex-E301-6.answer:
(a) Cooling capacity = electrical power input × COP

= 1500 × 2.3

= 3450 W

Amount of heat removed = cooling capacity × time

= 3450 × 60

= 2.07 × 105 J

(b) Rate of heat released to outside

= cooling capacity + electrical power input = 3450 + 1500 = 4950 W
ex-E301-6.location: Book E3  |  Chapter E301  |  Source PDF p. 29
